diagnosis_summary: The reviewed pre-fix source processed a loaded workflow during Workflow Entry initialization and could rewrite completion timestamps when no active activities remained. Rock closed the confirmed issue with commit 9db966e3da336b30ff62fffd1c54e147035922c5: the Obsidian block now returns the end-of-workflow result before processing a workflow that already has CompletedDateTime, and the legacy block likewise skips processing. The issue is labeled Fixed in v19.4; verify exact package inclusion because the label names a release line rather than an exact installed build.
workaround_summaries: When an existing completion timestamp is an audit or reporting datum, do not open that completed workflow through Workflow Entry. Use a read-only report or detail surface that does not process the workflow, and verify the chosen surface in staging.

verification_playbook.goal: Determine whether the installed build can reprocess completed workflows through Workflow Entry without risking a production timestamp change.
prerequisites: Know the exact installed Rock version or build ancestry.
Do not open a completed workflow through Workflow Entry while assessing an unverified build.

steps.title: Check build ancestry
steps.instructions: Confirm that the installed package contains commit 9db966e3da336b30ff62fffd1c54e147035922c5 or an independently verified equivalent fix.
steps.expected_if_affected: The installed build predates the guard or its Workflow Entry source still processes a workflow when CompletedDateTime already has a value.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The installed build contains the completed-workflow guard in both applicable Workflow Entry implementations.

steps.title: Count completed workflows without opening them
steps.instructions: Use the aggregate count only to determine whether completed workflows exist that could be exposed to the affected page. Do not return workflow IDs or other record details.
steps.probe: SELECT COUNT(*) AS CompletedWorkflowCount FROM [Workflow] WHERE [CompletedDateTime] IS NOT NULL
steps.expected_if_affected: A nonzero count establishes exposure if the installed build lacks the fix; it does not prove timestamps were already changed.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: A zero count means there is no current completed-workflow population to expose, while a fixed build removes the known processing path regardless of count.

limitations: There is no production-safe reproduction on an affected build because opening the target page is the action that can mutate the audit timestamp.
Historical data alone may not prove which page view changed a timestamp.

context.scope: completed workflows loaded through the Obsidian Workflow Entry block
exact Workflow Entry source revision; release package inclusion remains independently verifiable
official fix release line; verify the exact installed package
